To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
denervation rapidly (within one day) induces insulin resistance to glucose transport in rat hindlimbs, but does not alter glucose transporter number or expression.

denervation rapidly induces insulin resistance of glucose uptake in skeletal muscle, which is accompanied by a rapid (within 24 hours) decrease in GLUT-1 mRNA and a slower, more prolonged decrease in GLUT-4 protein.
the expression of GLUT4 is decreased in skeletal muscle after denervation, while the expression of GLUT1 is increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of glucose transport in skeletal muscle and the role of the nervous system in that process.
the molecular basis of denervation-induced insulin resistance of glucose utilization in skeletal muscle.
the effect of nerve injury on glucose metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
denervation induces a decrease in GLUT-4 expression and an increase in GLUT-1 expression, which are likely to contribute to the early postdenervation insulin resistance of glucose uptake.
denervation induces a rapid decrease in GLUT-4 expression in rat hindlimbs which is associated with insulin resistance of glucose metabolism.

denervation induces insulin resistance by a mechanism(s) that does not involve decreased GLUT-4 number; GLUT-4 number is decreased postdenervation but not to an extent that can account for the insulin resistance; and GLUT-1 number increases postdenervation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GLUT-1 and 4 mRNA and protein expression is differentially regulated in rat hindlimbs postdenervation.
the insulin resistance induced by denervation is associated with a decrease in GLUT-4 protein, which is probably regulated pretranslationally.

denervation induces an early (within 24-48 h) insulin-resistant state which is not due to changes in GLUT-1 or GLUT-4 expression; the insulin resistance is due to postreceptor defects in insulin signal transduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

denervation induces insulin resistance of glucose uptake in skeletal muscle and that this insulin resistance is not associated with a decrease in the total number of glucose transporter molecules in muscle.
the GLUT-4 glucose transporters in the muscle cells of rats are decreased by 50% after 3 days of denervation, and that GLUT-1 glucose transporters are upregulated by 60-100%.
denervation rapidly induces insulin resistance in muscle, but that this does not reflect a reduction in glucose transporters.
